3: ## Reverse Engineering Workflow
4: 
5: **When reverse engineering a function or any other element, always push your findings back to IDA.** This ensures the IDB stays up-to-date and serves as the single source of truth.
6: 
7: After analyzing code, use the appropriate tools to persist your discoveries:
8: 
9: | Finding | Tool to use |
10: |---|---|
11: | Function/variable purpose | `user-ida-pro-mcp-set_comments` |
12: | Better name for function | `user-ida-pro-mcp-rename` (key: `func`) |
13: | Better name for global | `user-ida-pro-mcp-rename` (key: `data`) |
14: | Better name for local var | `user-ida-pro-mcp-rename` (key: `local`) |
15: | Better name for stack var | `user-ida-pro-mcp-rename` (key: `stack`) |
16: | Type information | `user-ida-pro-mcp-set_type` |
17: | New struct/enum definition | `user-ida-pro-mcp-declare_type` |
18: | Stack variable declaration | `user-ida-pro-mcp-declare_stack` |
19: 
20: **Example workflow:**
21: 1. Decompile the function with `decompile`
22: 2. Analyze the code and understand its purpose
23: 3. Rename the function with a descriptive name via `rename`
24: 4. Add a comment explaining what it does via `set_comments`
25: 5. Rename local/stack variables to meaningful names via `rename`
26: 6. Set proper types for parameters and variables via `set_type`
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## IDA Pro MCP Tools
31: 
32: This project has an IDA Pro MCP server configured (`ida-pro-mcp` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`).
33: All IDA tools are available as **`user-ida-pro-mcp-*`** prefixed tool calls. Use them directly.
34: 
35: **Do NOT fall back to curl, HTTP requests, or Shell commands to reach IDA.** The tools work natively.
36: 
37: Common examples:
38: 
39: | Task | Tool call |
40: |---|---|
41: | Look up a function | `user-ida-pro-mcp-lookup_funcs` |
42: | Decompile | `user-ida-pro-mcp-decompile` |
43: | Call graph | `user-ida-pro-mcp-callgraph` |
44: | Cross-references | `user-ida-pro-mcp-xrefs_to` |
45: | Callees of a function | `user-ida-pro-mcp-callees` |
46: | Rename functions/globals | `user-ida-pro-mcp-rename` |
47: | List functions | `user-ida-pro-mcp-list_funcs` |
48: | Execute Python in IDA | `user-ida-pro-mcp-py_eval` |
49: 
50: The full API reference for parameters and return values is below.
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## MCP Resources
55: 
56: **Resources** represent browsable state (read-only data) following MCP's philosophy.
57: 
58: **Core IDB State:**
59: - `ida://idb/metadata` - IDB file info (path, arch, base, size, hashes)
60: - `ida://idb/segments` - Memory segments with permissions
61: - `ida://idb/entrypoints` - Entry points (main, TLS callbacks, etc.)
62: 
63: **UI State:**
64: - `ida://cursor` - Current cursor position and function
65: - `ida://selection` - Current selection range
66: 
67: **Type Information:**
68: - `ida://types` - All local types
69: - `ida://structs` - All structures/unions
70: - `ida://struct/{name}` - Structure definition with fields
71: 
72: **Lookups:**
73: - `ida://import/{name}` - Import details by name
74: - `ida://export/{name}` - Export details by name
75: - `ida://xrefs/from/{addr}` - Cross-references from address
76: 
77: ## Core Functions
78: 
79: - `lookup_funcs(queries)`: Get function(s) by address or name (auto-detects, accepts list or comma-separated string).
80: - `int_convert(inputs)`: Convert numbers to different formats (decimal, hex, bytes, ASCII, binary).
81: - `list_funcs(queries)`: List functions (paginated, filtered).
82: - `list_globals(queries)`: List global variables (paginated, filtered).
83: - `imports(offset, count)`: List all imported symbols with module names (paginated).
84: - `decompile(addr)`: Decompile function at the given address.
85: - `disasm(addr)`: Disassemble function with full details (arguments, stack frame, etc).
86: - `xrefs_to(addrs)`: Get all cross-references to address(es).
87: - `xrefs_to_field(queries)`: Get cross-references to specific struct field(s).
88: - `callees(addrs)`: Get functions called by function(s) at address(es).
89: 
90: ## Modification Operations
91: 
92: - `set_comments(items)`: Set comments at address(es) in both disassembly and decompiler views.
93: - `patch_asm(items)`: Patch assembly instructions at address(es).
94: - `declare_type(decls)`: Declare C type(s) in the local type library.
95: 
96: ## Memory Reading Operations
97: 
98: - `get_bytes(addrs)`: Read raw bytes at address(es).
99: - `get_int(queries)`: Read integer values using ty (i8/u64/i16le/i16be/etc).
100: - `get_string(addrs)`: Read null-terminated string(s).
101: - `get_global_value(queries)`: Read global variable value(s) by address or name (auto-detects, compile-time values).
102: 
103: ## Stack Frame Operations
104: 
105: - `stack_frame(addrs)`: Get stack frame variables for function(s).
106: - `declare_stack(items)`: Create stack variable(s) at specified offset(s).
107: - `delete_stack(items)`: Delete stack variable(s) by name.
108: 
109: ## Structure Operations
110: 
111: - `read_struct(queries)`: Read structure field values at specific address(es).
112: - `search_structs(filter)`: Search structures by name pattern.
113: 
114: ## Debugger Operations (Extension)
115: 
116: Debugger tools are hidden by default. Enable with `?ext=dbg` query parameter:
117: 
118: ```
119: http://127.0.0.1:13337/mcp?ext=dbg
120: ```
121: 
122: **Control:**
123: - `dbg_start()`: Start debugger process.
124: - `dbg_exit()`: Exit debugger process.
125: - `dbg_continue()`: Continue execution.
126: - `dbg_run_to(addr)`: Run to address.
127: - `dbg_step_into()`: Step into instruction.
128: - `dbg_step_over()`: Step over instruction.
129: 
130: **Breakpoints:**
131: - `dbg_bps()`: List all breakpoints.
132: - `dbg_add_bp(addrs)`: Add breakpoint(s).
133: - `dbg_delete_bp(addrs)`: Delete breakpoint(s).
134: - `dbg_toggle_bp(items)`: Enable/disable breakpoint(s).
135: 
136: **Registers:**
137: - `dbg_regs()`: All registers, current thread.
138: - `dbg_regs_all()`: All registers, all threads.
139: - `dbg_regs_remote(tids)`: All registers, specific thread(s).
140: - `dbg_gpregs()`: GP registers, current thread.
141: - `dbg_gpregs_remote(tids)`: GP registers, specific thread(s).
142: - `dbg_regs_named(names)`: Named registers, current thread.
143: - `dbg_regs_named_remote(tid, names)`: Named registers, specific thread.
144: 
145: **Stack & Memory:**
146: - `dbg_stacktrace()`: Call stack with module/symbol info.
147: - `dbg_read(regions)`: Read memory from debugged process.
148: - `dbg_write(regions)`: Write memory to debugged process.
149: 
150: ## Advanced Analysis Operations
151: 
152: - `py_eval(code)`: Execute arbitrary Python code in IDA context (returns dict with result/stdout/stderr, supports Jupyter-style evaluation).
153: - `analyze_funcs(addrs)`: Comprehensive function analysis (decompilation, assembly, xrefs, callees, callers, strings, constants, basic blocks).
154: 
155: ## Pattern Matching & Search
156: 
157: - `find_regex(queries)`: Search strings with case-insensitive regex (paginated).
158: - `find_bytes(patterns, limit=1000, offset=0)`: Find byte pattern(s) in binary (e.g., "48 8B ?? ??"). Max limit: 10000.
159: - `find_insns(sequences, limit=1000, offset=0)`: Find instruction sequence(s) in code. Max limit: 10000.
160: - `find(type, targets, limit=1000, offset=0)`: Advanced search (immediate values, strings, data/code references). Max limit: 10000.
161: 
162: ## Control Flow Analysis
163: 
164: - `basic_blocks(addrs)`: Get basic blocks with successors and predecessors.
165: 
166: ## Type Operations
167: 
168: - `set_type(edits)`: Apply type(s) to functions, globals, locals, or stack variables.
169: - `infer_types(addrs)`: Infer types at address(es) using Hex-Rays or heuristics.
170:

172: 
173: - `export_funcs(addrs, format)`: Export function(s) in specified format (json, c_header, or prototypes).
174:

176: 
177: - `callgraph(roots, max_depth)`: Build call graph from root function(s) with configurable depth.
